hints: Focus on where Na, Mg, Al and Si sit in the Periodic Table, they are all in Period 3 from left to right.
Recall how atomic radius changes across a period, Na is largest and Si is smallest because nuclear charge increases.
Now link radius to electronegativity, the smallest atom holds bonding electrons most strongly, so check which graph has opposite trends for the two properties.
walkthrough:
**Spot the period trend for atomic radius**

These four elements are Period 3 in order: Na, Mg, Al, Si. Across the period, protons are added but shielding stays similar, so the stronger nuclear pull shrinks the atom.

Radius order (largest to smallest):
$$\text{Na} > \text{Mg} > \text{Al} > \text{Si}$$

**Spot the period trend for electronegativity**

Electronegativity is the attraction for a shared pair in a bond. A smaller atom with higher nuclear charge pulls more strongly, so it increases across the period.

Electronegativity order (lowest to highest):
$$\text{Na} < \text{Mg} < \text{Al} < \text{Si}$$

**Combine the two trends on the graph**

The x-axis is atomic radius (increasing to the right) and the y-axis is electronegativity (increasing upwards. So Na must be bottom right (big radius, low EN) and Si must be top left (small radius, high EN), with Mg and Al in between in order. Only one graph shows this smooth downhill pattern.

options.A: Correct. Na is furthest right and lowest (largest radius, lowest electronegativity), then Mg, then Al, then Si is furthest left and highest (smallest radius, highest electronegativity). This matches both Period 3 trends perfectly.
options.B: Incorrect. The left to right order for radius (Si, Al, Mg, Na) is correct, but Si is plotted with very low electronegativity. In reality Si has the highest nuclear charge of the four and the smallest radius, so it should have the highest electronegativity, not the lowest.
options.C: Incorrect. This graph shows electronegativity increasing as atomic radius increases, with Na highest and Si lowest. That is the exact opposite of the true trend. It is a common trap if you confuse the group trend (down a group) with the period trend (across a period).
options.D: Incorrect. The vertical order for electronegativity (Na < Mg < Al < Si) is correct, but the horizontal order for radius is wrong because Al is shown smaller than Si. Si must be smaller than Al due to greater proton number, so this swap rules the graph out.
